# Jobs reference

Every class in `assets/scripts/jobs/`, from its doc comments. The overview is in [README.md](README.md).

- [TickJobs](#tickjobs)

## TickJobs

`res://assets/scripts/jobs/TickJobs.gd`, extends [`RefCounted`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_refcounted.html)

Finds the one job scheduler every job kind shares (scaling spec section 4).

The scheduler itself is C++ (JobScheduler in navcore): worker threads that take batches of plain-data work, such as the sensing job (AISensingJob), from one shared queue. This class only holds it, so any script can find it, and keeps the two settings a game or a test might change.

Not an autoload and never instanced: everything here is static (few autoloads). GDScript note: a static var belongs to the class, not to an object, so there's one of each for the whole game, like Pawn's shared table.

Without the C++ library, `get_scheduler()` returns null and every job kind runs on the main thread instead.

### Settings and properties

- `enabled: bool` = `true`: Off: no jobs, and every job kind runs on the main thread. On by default; read when each part is ready, so set it before pawns are made.

### Functions

- `get_scheduler() -> Object` *(static)*: The shared scheduler, or null without the C++ library or with enabled off.
- `set_worker_count(count: int) -> void` *(static)*: How many worker threads: -1 (the default) sizes it to the machine (scaling spec 4.1: its cores, minus one for the main thread, minus one more if this machine also draws the game, at most 8); 0 means none, so every job runs on the main thread when its result is needed; any other number fixes it, as tests do so they repeat on any machine. The answers are the same with any number.
- `get_worker_count_setting() -> int` *(static)*: The worker count last set with `set_worker_count()`: -1 means sized to the machine.
